correctness.rationale: Derived p0=c=(1-q)(1-r)/(1-qr), pk=c(q^k+r^k) for k>=1 from the two disjoint diagonals of X-Y. G(z)=c(1-qr z^2)/[(1-qz)(1-rz)]; logarithm expansion gives nonnegative nu_odd and nu_even, summable since q,r<1 and G(1)=1. Bouzar Prop 1 applies since p0>0 and the law is compound Poisson: the canonical sequence a_k=k nu_k must be nonincreasing. Every odd-to-even step decreases; each even-to-following-odd inequality is (q^m-r^m)^2 >= q^(2m+1)+r^(2m+1). With q>=r,t=r/q<=1 its left (1-t^m)^2 increases, right q(1+t^(2m+1)) decreases, so all m iff m=1, yielding the displayed sharp included boundary. For k>=2, p(k-1)p(k+1)-p(k)^2=c^2(qr)^(k-1)(q-r)^2, and k=1 minor p1^2-p0p2=2c^2qr>0: log-concavity only at symmetry, incompatible with threshold. Independent exact Fraction tests checked examples on both sides plus symmetry; finite examples are not proof of the all-m iff statement.

value.rationale: The absolute magnitude |X-Y| is a standard observable for paired count differences, but folding does not preserve signed convolution representations. A complete two-dimensional, equality-inclusive cubic thinning phase boundary with an explicit parity-sensitive Levy measure is a useful structural classification of discrete distributions, clearly separating ID, thinning SD, and log-concavity; it is not solely a reparametrized example of the general criterion.
